source.title: Does Fine-Tuning Undo Activation Steering? Behavioural Recovery Without Weight-Edit Reversal
source.authors: Philipp E. Glass; Allan Tucker; Yong-Min Li; A. Miron

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether fine-tuning preserves deliberately embedded activation steering, not whether fine-tuning safety-trained models on harmful or benign examples causes the claimed safety loss. Its refusal behavior is measured after intentionally ablating refusal, so it does not test the versions as defined.
record.gate_note: The paper reports refusal-rate outcomes after SFT and RLHF on models whose refusal behavior was intentionally suppressed by embedded steering. These are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version, not as tests of the claim versions. The paper does not measure first-token KL, compliant prefilling, suffixes, decoding changes, safety-localized parameters, why safety is shallow, or deepening safety.
record.test_reason: The study's main experiments (rows R1–R12) are on models whose refusal was deliberately ablated, so they test none of the versions. Its Appendix B control, however, fine-tunes the unmodified safety-trained models on benign OpenOrca data with full-parameter SFT and reports refusal on 100 harmful prompts. That result bears directly on V2, in a new setting (full-parameter SFT, 1,024 steps, five open models).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also stress that the weight edit itself persists (mean ρ=0.004; at most 0.79% reversed) even when behaviour recovers. They add that, as a control, benign SFT leaves refusal in unsteered models nearly unchanged.
record.recipe_differences: Studies full-parameter SFT and RLHF after embedding activation steering in weights; it does not reproduce fine-tuning aligned models on harmful or benign examples to measure safety loss.
record.method_sensitivity: Refusal recovery differed between SFT and RLHF and across models. The authors associate the pattern with training-data signals opposing refusal ablation, but use only one dataset per training paradigm and do not systematically vary the amount of contradictory signal.

fits_no_version.finding: After refusal is deliberately ablated via a weight edit, benign SFT restores refusal partway (mean 0.06→0.61), while RLHF on hh-rlhf leaves it low (0.07). Both happen with less than 2% of the edit reversed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Routine fine-tuning can restore refusal suppressed by embedded steering, without undoing the weight edit, depending on the training signal against it.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing; the text states accepted to the EMNLP 2026 Main Conference.
record.problems: The study uses one dataset per training paradigm and does not systematically vary contradictory training signal. It covers five models up to 14B parameters and full-parameter fine-tuning only. Refusal classification uses an LLM judge, with cross-validation but residual misclassification not ruled out. The study does not identify the pathways underlying behavioral recovery.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for brevity amplification: it measures response length rather than refusal or harmful compliance. No rows for vector recovery, cosine similarity, or weight-edit reversal: these measure edit persistence, not the behaviors named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Refusal after RLHF on non-steered models is not reported; Appendix B gives only brevity for RLHF. Carefully selected benign data and small-sample benign fine-tuning are not tested. LoRA is not tested.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
A refusal direction is ablated on purpose. The study does not test whether a small set of weights carries safety.

missing.what: Refusal rate of unsteered safety-trained models before and after benign OpenOrca SFT, for all five models: base 0.97/0.96/0.98/0.99/0.60 and SFT 0.99/0.99/0.96/0.98/0.79 (mean 0.90→0.94).

record.verdict_notes: The record's T6/discusses classification overlooks the Appendix B control. That control is the only part of the study bearing on the claim: it is a V2-relevant null result that benign full-parameter SFT does not erode refusal. The study cites Qi et al. (one of the original sources) only in passing. The steered-model rows rightly carry no versions, because the reduced compliance there is induced deliberately.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune safety-trained models on harmful examples or test whether such training removes refusal.
Does not test whether benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance in safety-trained models; SFT is applied after deliberate refusal ablation.
No per-token KL analysis between aligned and base models.
No tests of compliant prefilling, suffix attacks, or decoding changes.
Measures persistence of an embedded steering edit, not whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Does not test whether data or training objectives cause first-token concentration or safety shallowness.
Does not train safety across response positions or test whether such deepening holds up.

rows.check: Linking to none is correct. The paper's 'complete reversal' means refusal recovered to the unsteered base (0.62 vs base 0.60, Psft −0.04). That is recovery from the ablation, not a safety-loss effect.

rows.subject: Mean (five evaluated models)
rows.operation_detail: SFT on OpenOrca after embedded refusal ablation; aggregate reported across five models
rows.note: The unsteered base mean was 0.90. The paper reports mean behavioral recovery of 69% for refusal ablation.
rows.check: Aggregate row duplicating R1–R9. Its 69% recovery equals 1 − mean Psft (0.31). It is acceptable but should not be counted as independent evidence.

relationships.condition: Full-parameter SFT on OpenOrca (1,024 steps) of unsteered Llama-3.2-3B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3-8B, Qwen3-14B and SOLAR-10.7B; refusal judged on 100 harmful prompts.
relationships.reason: Based on the text (Appendix B, Table 4), since no row records it. Mean refusal went from 0.90 to 0.94 after benign SFT; per model: 0.97→0.99, 0.96→0.99, 0.98→0.96, 0.99→0.98, 0.60→0.79. That is no erosion of safety, and refusal rose for SOLAR. Caveat: OpenOrca contains about 0.1% refusal completions, and no CIs are given for these values.
relationships.display_finding: Mean refusal rose from 0.90 to 0.94 after benign SFT, with per-model values of 0.97→0.99, 0.96→0.99, 0.98→0.96, 0.99→0.98 and 0.60→0.79, and refusal rose for SOLAR. OpenOrca contains about 0.1% refusal completions, and no confidence intervals are given.
